newsitem.title: UK: Wolseley climbs on buy recommendation.
newsitem.headline: Wolseley climbs on buy recommendation.

text.p: Shares in Wolseley Plc, a UK distributor of building, plumbing and bathroom materials, rose on Friday after Credit Lyonnais Laing recommended the stock as a buy, along with other firms in the building sector.
At 1510 GMT, Wolseley shares were up 11-1/2p at 459 - a 2.6 percent increase which even out-performed the firm FTSE 100.
Credit Lyonnais Laing's Mike Foster said they saw momentum gathering in the building sector and a turnaround in sentiment.
"We are particularly keen on the merchanting sector because we've seen strength in the UK second-hand housing market since the spring," said Foster, an analyst at the brokerage.
Foster said a report out on Thursday from the Royal Institute of Chartered Surveyors showed November turnover figures to be the highest for the year.
"Trading in UK merchants was bad in 1995 and 1996, but the rate of decline ended three months ago. We expect an upturn in 1997 based on the strength of the 1996 housing market," he said.
Foster said Laing was not upgrading its pre-tax profit forecast for Wolseley, which was recently downgraded to 250 million stg for the year to December 1996 on currency woes.
Wolseley makes around 70 percent of its profit overseas, and about 50 percent in the U.S. where people expect a downturn in the booming housing market.
But Foster said he thought the U.S. downturn would be moderate. "We strongly believe Wolseley's dollar profits won't fall - they're well placed in the U.S.," he said.
Laing also recommended building materials and paper manufacturer BPB and building materials distributor Travis Perkins, which both saw their shares up sharply.
